title: Run kinetic Monte Carlo crystal growth simulations
action: Implement the kinetic Monte Carlo crystal growth model on a 2D trigonal lattice following Xiao et al. (1988) as adapted by the studied paper. Include random-walk diffusion of a single effective growth species from a circular source region, surface attachment kinetics with probabilities from interaction energy E_i = Φ₁ n_i + Φ₂ m_i (nearest and next-nearest neighbors), and surface diffusion along crystal faces. Use fixed normalized bond strengths Φ₁/kT = 7, Φ₂/Φ₁ = 0.1. Run a set of at least 8 constant-Δμ/kT simulations spanning values from ~0.01 to ~10. For each, after sufficient growth steps, record the final crystal occupancy grid and compute branch count and compactness (e.g., circularity 4π·area/perimeter²). Also run one time‑varying simulation where log₁₀(Δμ/kT) decreases linearly from 0.7 to -2 (or equivalent) over the growth history. Save computed branch counts, compactness, and the final grid from the variable run into intermediate_results.json.
description: Core simulation stage; generates raw morphology data needed for subsequent analysis.
output_schema: JSON with runs list and variable_grid.

title: Compile morphology table
action: From the intermediate simulation results (intermediate_results.json), create a CSV table with columns: run_id, delta_mu_kT, branch_count, compactness. Include all constant-supersaturation runs and the variable-overstepping run.
description: Table of morphological descriptors across all simulation conditions.
output_schema: CSV with columns: run_id (string), delta_mu_kT (float, empty for variable run), branch_count (int), compactness (float).

title: Estimate morphological transition threshold
action: Using branch_count vs. Δμ/kT data from the constant runs, determine the dimensionless supersaturation at which branching disappears (branch_count ≤ 1). Write the estimated threshold to a plain text file.
description: Estimated transition supersaturation; depends on actual simulation outcomes and cannot be obtained without running the simulations.

title: Save final grid for variable overstepping run
action: Save the final crystal occupancy grid from the time-varying Δμ/kT simulation (stored in intermediate_results.json) into a plain text file.
output_schema: Space-separated integers (0 or 1), row-major order; grid dimensions determined by simulation.
